# grr

> grr is a zero-config Rust CLI for Google Workspace. One binary, one OAuth login, and a command tree generated from Google's Discovery Service: 401 methods across 14 APIs (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, People, Chat, Forms, Tasks, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Apps Script, Analytics Admin, Analytics Data, Search Console) as namespaced subcommands — `grr gmail users messages list`, `grr calendar events list`, `grr drive files list` — with typed kebab-case flags per method, bodies via `--params`/`--body-file`, and `grr api list|describe|call|refresh` as the flat escape hatch. Results are JSON on stdout and logs on stderr, so `grr … | jq` works. Release binaries ship with an OAuth client compiled in; `grr auth login` is all that is needed.

## Agent skill

- [skills/grr/SKILL.md](https://github.com/debanjanbasu/grr-cli/blob/main/skills/grr/SKILL.md): The packaged agent skill — the discovery-first discipline (`grr schema` → `grr api list` → `grr api describe` → `--dry-run`), the method-id naming rule, the typed-flag rules, and the output contract. Install into any harness with `npx skills add https://github.com/debanjanbasu/grr-cli`.
- [skills/<service>/SKILL.md](https://github.com/debanjanbasu/grr-cli/tree/main/skills): One generated skill per service (14) - load progressively alongside the core skill; each covers its method surface, examples, and scope caveats, baked from the same discovery index.

## Agent surfaces

- [MCP server](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/commands/): `grr mcp` serves a Model Context Protocol stdio server exposing every one of the 401 methods as a typed MCP tool; `--readonly` for a read-only server.
- [Natural language](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/commands/): `grr ask "show my unread messages"` - a System One model (Jev by default) classifies the request hierarchically and fills the typed parameters; prints the plan, `--run` executes.
- [Safety profiles](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/commands/): global `--readonly`, `--deny-service`, `--deny-verb` flags honored by the CLI, `grr api call`, and the MCP server alike.
- [Multi-account](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/commands/): `grr auth login --account work` keeps a separate token per account in the OS keyring.
- [Terminal demo](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/): an asciinema cast of real output, including an opencode agent driving grr.
## Docs

- [Docs](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/): Documentation index. One generated command tree, the id-based `grr api` surface over the same index, and which to use.
- [Getting started](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/getting-started/): Install on macOS, Linux, or Windows (incl. the required Homebrew `trust` step and winget), `grr auth login`, first command, and verifying with `grr auth status` and `grr transport`.
- [Commands](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/commands/): The naming rule that predicts any command from its method id, the typed-flag rules, per-service examples for all 14 services, and the account-level commands.
- [Discovery API](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/discovery/): `grr api list` / `describe` / `call` / `refresh`, the 401-method coverage table across 14 APIs, `--dry-run`, per-method least-privilege scopes, and the Tasks scope caveat.
- [Agents and harnesses](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/docs/agents/): The contract for AI agents and coding harnesses — parse stdout not stderr, discover with `grr schema` and `grr api list` rather than assuming, `--dry-run` before writes, and keyring token storage. Includes the packaged skill and a copy-pasteable agent quickstart.

## Optional

- [Overview](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/): What grr is, the 14 services, the architecture, and answers to common questions.
- [Compare](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/compare/): Measured startup, binary size, and request latency against the other Google Workspace CLIs, refreshed daily.
- [Install](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/install/): Release channels, archive formats and sizes, crates.io and source builds, and OAuth setup.
- [Privacy](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/privacy/): Credential and token storage, what the CLI sends, and what this static site does not do.
- [Terms](https://grr-cli.pages.dev/terms/): Project terms, licensing, and the no-endorsement statement.
